canonical_question: What specific grain size range constitutes the 'high density of stable grain boundaries' that leads to the observed 'grain refinement'?

question_variants.question: What specific grain size range constitutes the 'high density of stable grain boundaries' that leads to the observed 'grain refinement'?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text confirms grain refinement occurred under dual-beam irradiation and mentions 'high density of stable grain boundaries', but it does not specify the numerical grain size range associated with this description.

answers.answer: The evidence states that grain refinement occurred but does not provide a specific numerical range for the grain size or define the exact range of grain boundary density that constitutes 'high density'.
answers.conditions: in situ real-time, 0.25 dpa, He + heavy ions
answers.mechanism: overlapping cascades larger than grain size
answers.boundary_limitation: No specific grain size range quantified in the text
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time
